title: Applied ML Eval Harness & Onboarding — End-to-End Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's applied-ML evaluation practices and runbooks into a single, end-to-end guide. It covers the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmark design, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile requirements, and the regression triage playbook. The intent is to give ML engineers and reviewers a single reference for safely introducing, validating, and operating model variants in production.

Scope

- Audience: ML Engineers, Applied ML, Model Ops, SRE, and Product owners.
- Systems covered: eval-harness (bench-runner), model-registry, CI gating (github actions), metrics-store (Influx/Prometheus + Timescale), artifact storage (s3://redwood-evals), and alerting channels (PagerDuty + #applied-ml-alerts).
- Outcomes: reproducible evaluations, automatic gating on quality regressions, clear triage steps, and approved quantization profiles before rollout.

High-level workflow

1) Author creates/updates prompt sets and benchmark definitions.
2) Author submits model in model-registry with metadata and quantization candidates.
3) CI triggers eval-harness: runs functional tests, benchmark suites, and quality guardrail checks.
4) Results are recorded to metrics-store and evaluation artifacts to s3.
5) Automated gating determines pass/fail; failures trigger regression-triage playbook.
6) On pass, model is tagged for canary rollout per rollout policy.

Ownership and contacts

- Eval harness owners: Applied ML team (oncall: @applied-ml-oncall).
- Model onboarding steward: Model Platform (owner: Clara Jensen).
- Regression triage owner: Applied ML (lead: Marcus Lee).
- Quantization profiles owner: Serving Runtime (lead: Daniel Ortiz).

Eval harness: standards and expectations

Purpose: Provide reproducible, fast, and comparable measurements for model behavior on production-like workloads. The harness supports deterministic workloads (unit tests), prompt-set benchmarks, and smoke tests for kv-cache correctness and latency profiling.

Key properties
- Determinism: seeds and env locked for unit tests; default seed=42.
- Run modes: quick (subset, ~5–10 min), full (all benchmarks, variable runtime), and nightly (expanded cross-run comparisons).
- Artifact retention: artifacts kept for 90 days by default (s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{model}/{run-id}).
- Metadata captured: model-id, model-commit, quantization-profile-id, dataset-version, prompt-set-id, runner-version, hw-profile.

CLI examples

- Run quick suite: ri-eval run --mode quick --model model-123 --prompt-set ps-translate-v1
- Submit to CI: ri-eval submit --model model-123 --profile q8_ggml --benchmarks all --notify #applied-ml-alerts

Prompt sets and benchmarks: design guidelines

- Prompt set format: JSONL with fields: id, task, input, expected_output (optional), tags. See example below.
- Coverage matrix: ensure prompt sets span intent types, length buckets (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, 512+), rare-token rates, and safety-sensitive categories.
- Benchmark composition: include functional correctness (exact match / F1), helpfulness/style metrics (human eval or automated proxies), safety checks (toxicity, PII leakage), and embedding-similarity for retrieval tasks.
- Versioning: every prompt set update must include changelog and dataset-version tag.

Example prompt-set JSONL (single line format)

{"id":"ps-translate-v1-0001","task":"translate","input":"How are you?","expected_output":"¿Cómo estás?","tags":["translate","short"]}

Benchmark metrics and thresholds

- Core metrics (examples):
  - exact_match (EM): pass threshold >= 92% for model-stable releases.
  - f1_score: used for QA where EM is brittle; pass threshold >= 0.86.
  - helpfulness_auto (LM-based proxy): relative drop vs baseline < 2.5%.
  - toxicity_rate: must be <= 0.5% on safety prompt set.
  - latency_p50/p95: must meet per-tier SLOs (hosted api p95 <= 700ms for 8k context on standard tier).

- Gate types: hard gates (safety, export compliance, data-leakage) and soft gates (helpfulness degradation, small accuracy drops). Hard gates must pass; soft gates allow exceptions with explicit signoff.

Model onboarding checklist (must be completed before canary)

1) Register model in model-registry with descriptive metadata and owner contact.
2) Provide artifact bundle including: model weights link, tokenizer spec, config.json, supported context lengths, and quantization candidates.
3) Submit eval-harness run (full suite) and attach artifact links.
4) Fill onboarding metadata template: expected latencies, memory footprint, recommended quantization profile, known failure modes.
5) Security & data review: confirm no training data with restricted PII, signoff from security if needed.
6) Quality review: Applied ML approver signs off if soft gates exceeded with mitigation plan.

Quality guardrails: automated and human reviews

- Automated guardrails: safety checks (toxicity classifiers), PII detectors (regex + model-based), prompt injection tests, hallucination proxy tests (answer plausibility heuristics), and regression-to-baseline checks.
- Human review: targeted human evaluations for any safety-sensitive or large soft-gate regressions. Human evals must be recorded with dataset-version and annotation protocol.
- Monitoring: after rollout, continuous monitoring tracks eval-metrics on live traffic sample (1% by default). Alerts on 3-sigma deviations or when metric crosses gate thresholds.

Quantization profiles: required metadata and sample

Each quantization profile must include the following flat metadata fields (stored in model-registry as strings):
- profile_id, description, bitwidths, per-layer-exceptions, supported_hardware, expected_size_reduction, known_accuracy_delta.

Example quantization profile (YAML described inline):

profile_id: q8_ggml
description: 8-bit symmetric quantization with per-block scaling, default for low-cost experiments
bitwidths: 8
per-layer-exceptions: none
supported_hardware: a100_v5,gpu_xeon32
expected_size_reduction: 4x
known_accuracy_delta: "~1.8% EM drop on translation baseline"

Quantization validation steps:

1) Run quantized candidate through eval-harness full suite.
2) Confirm hard gates and acceptable soft gate deltas.
3) Run performance benchmarks (throughput and latency) on target hardware using bench-runner.
4) Approve profile in model-registry and attach artifacts.

Regression triage playbook (on CI or runtime alerts)

Immediate actions (first 30 minutes):
1) Acknowledge alert and create incident in incident tracker with run-id and model-id.
2) Pull eval-harness artifacts and reproduce failing benchmark locally using same runner-version and seed.
3) Compare metrics vs baseline; capture diff and top-failing prompt examples (at least 10).
4) If reproducible, escalate to applied-ml oncall and assign owner.

Investigation steps (0.5–6 hours):
1) Check metadata differences: model-commit, quantization-profile, prompt-set-version, runner-version, and hw-profile.
2) Run targeted A/B on small sample to isolate regression source (model vs infra vs tokenization).
3) For quantization-related regressions, test full-precision candidate to verify accuracy restoration.
4) Document root cause and recommended rollback or mitigation.

Resolution and follow-up (6 hours–7 days):
1) If rollback required, follow rollback playbook: pin traffic to previous model tag, notify stakeholders, and schedule postmortem.
2) If fixable without rollback, deploy hotfix and run accelerated evaluation to confirm.
3) Postmortem must include timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and owner for each action item.

CI gating and automation patterns

- Gate runs: every model change triggers a quick suite; PRs with model changes require passing quick suite to merge.
- Release pipeline: full suite + nightlies required before tagging a production candidate.
- Automations: use GitHub Actions + ri-eval action to run harness; on failure auto-open triage ticket template.

Metrics dashboard and alerting

- Dashboards: per-model pages showing core eval metrics, trend lines, per-prompt-failure heatmaps, and latency breakdowns.
- Alerts: PagerDuty for hard gate failures; slack channel for soft gate regressions with a weekly digest.

Appendices

A. Example minimal onboarding metadata template (YAML inline)
model_id: model-123
owner: ml-team
context_window: 8192
recommended_quant_profiles: [q8_ggml, q4_opt]

B. Prompt set quality checklist

- Diversity: includes multiple languages and domains.
- Edge cases: includes truncation and special token tests.
- Safety: includes targeted adversarial prompts.
- Traceability: every prompt links to source and curator.

C. Useful commands and locations

- Eval artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/artifacts/{model}/{run-id}
- Model registry UI: https://model-registry.internal.redwood/
- Run quick locally: ri-eval run --mode quick --model {model-id} --prompt-set {ps-id}

D. Frequently asked questions

Q: What if a soft gate is missed but measured drop is small?
A: Escalate to Applied ML for a risk assessment; a documented mitigation plan and temporary traffic limits can be applied while additional testing completes.

Q: How long are prompt sets retained?
A: Prompt sets and versions are retained indefinitely in dataset storage, with snapshots exported for reproducibility.

Summary

This guide centralizes the best practices and operational playbooks for applied-ML evaluations at Redwood. Follow the workflows for reproducible evaluation, strict safety gating, and rapid but controlled rollouts. For questions or updates to this playbook, contact the Applied ML owners listed above and submit a change request via the model-registry change workflow.
